OpenAI just announced a model specifically built for vulnerability research, while video generation costs drop by another 30%.

Here are the key technical updates from today across model development and AI engineering tools.

🛡️ OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model engineered to identify exploitable software vulnerabilities and develop fixes while operating strictly within authorized scope.

🎥 Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, bringing video generation costs down by 30% to $0.07 per second of 720p video. The model supports native 15-second clip generation and multi-turn conversational editing.

🤖 Perplexity launched Teammates, always-on workplace agents that pull memory, skills, and context from existing workspace projects. The agents integrate with Perplexity Computer to deploy directly on user devices.

✏️ Google updated Gemini Canvas with a sketch-to-app feature, allowing developers to upload hand-drawn diagrams and instantly generate or refine functional application code.

The shift toward target-specific models like GPT-6 Cyber indicates how frontier providers are tailoring base architectures for strict operational boundaries. Meanwhile, video synthesis dropping to seven cents per second lowers the cost threshold for automated media generation in production applications.

From an engineering perspective, local agent execution and direct visual-to-code compilation reflect a clear trend toward tighter integration into everyday developer workflows.
